newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks rise on Dow record, gold bounce.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks rise on Dow record, gold bounce.

text.p: Australian shares opened firmer on Wednesday after a fresh record on Wall Street and firm buying in gold shares after a small bounce in bullion price.
Within 30 minutes of the opening, the key All Ordinaries index was 12.2 points up at 2,691.4 with about A$430 million (US$320 million) worth of trade going through the market.
Trade was boosted by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp sale of its entire 40 percent stake in magazine publisher PMP Communications Ltd, which raised about A$320 million for News.

Brokers said investors were starting to buy shares at lower prices after four days of price falls led by the battered gold price following the sale by Australia's central bank of two-thirds of its gold reserves last Thursday.
"The whole market looks good. There are few bargain hunters in there, as there was a bit of panic selling yesterday," said Gordon Furner, an institutional dealer at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.

Furner said gold stocks were in demand as investors took some confidence in the slight bounce to the bullion price offshore. COMEX August gold ended up US$2.00 at $321.00 an ounce, after hitting a low of $314.60 on Monday.
"Gold stocks are looking a lot better," Furner said.
Gold miners Acacia Resources, Normandy Mining and Lihir Gold were all among the most actively traded stocks, with each priced higher than Tuesday's close.
The September share price index futures contracts was 13 points higher at 2,718, a 26.6 point premium to the underlying index.
